newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila businessmen urge change in forex policy.
newsitem.headline: Manila businessmen urge change in forex policy.

text.p: A group of Filipino businessmen on Friday reiterated their demand that the monetary authority should allow the peso to depreciate in order to enhance the export competitiveness of local industries.

The Federation of Philippine Industries and the Philippine Exporters Confederation made the suggestion during a forum between the Department of Trade and Industry and industry leaders, Trade Secretary Cesar Bautista said.

Bautista, who is also a member of the Monetary Board, rejected the proposal and said it would be unwise for the government to peg the peso at a lower rate against the dollar, since it would be best to let market forces decide the exchange rate.
The Central Bank freed up foreign exchange regulations in 1992. The peso has remained relatively strong at around 26 pesos to a dollar against the previous 27 to 28.
The business groups said a strong peso had hurt their competitive advantage in the international market.
Bautista said he had asked industry leaders to look at other factors, such as labour and power costs and tariff rates, in which the government might be willing to help.
